text:
Maria S (Support): customer reporting a spike in 502/504s from hosted API over the last ~30m. says errors cluster around 3xx -> TLS handshake timeouts. attaching sample logs from their side.
Olivia C (Customer Success): I have the account details: acct-redwood-42, started hitting issues at 02:12 UTC, affects multiple regions (us-west, eu-west) but not all requests.
Maria S (Support): quick repro curl from their network: `curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate` -> TLS handshake timeout.
Maria S (Support): their traceroute shows last hop going to old-gw-1.example.net in us-west.
Jonas R (Eng-Runtime): that old-gw host should have been decommissioned during the September edge migration. can you paste the exact IP?
Maria S (Support): 54.152.201.98
Lee K (Eng-SRE): checking our DNS history... looks like dns cache at their resolver still returns CNAME -> old-gw.* for some queries. dig +trace from my laptop gives correct CNAME chain to new-edge-1.redwood.net, but from their provided dig output it resolves to old-gw.
Olivia C (Customer Success): customer says their corporate resolver enforces long TTLs and only flushes nightly.
Jonas R (Eng-Runtime): that could explain intermittent hits to retired gateway with expired certs. old-gw cert expired 2026-02-28. If traffic reaches it, TLS handshake will fail or time out.
pagerduty: Incident #INC-8791 created and assigned to eng-sre oncall.
Lee K (Eng-SRE): collecting envoy / haproxy logs around 02:10-02:20 UTC across the edge pool.
Lee K (Eng-SRE): snippet from old-gw (archived): `TLS handshake timeout from 10.23.45.67: remote closed` and `certificate verify failed: certificate has expired`
Jonas R (Eng-Runtime): so customer hits old IP -> cert expired -> TLS handshake hangs -> client retries -> gateway returns 502/504. makes sense.
Maria S (Support): the customer asked if we rotated certs incorrectly last night. any rotational activity?
Jonas R (Eng-Runtime): we performed a controlled rollover for new-edge cert chain at 01:45 UTC. rollout target was new-edge hosts only; old-gw was scheduled for teardown but should not be in DNS anymore.
Lee K (Eng-SRE): action plan: 1) purge stale A/CNAME entries from global DNS and CDN, 2) confirm BGP/edge decommission completed, 3) add a temporary redirect from old-gw IPs to new-edge while customers finish TTLs.
Maria S (Support): can we get a safe rollforward so customer traffic isn't hitting expired certs? they are willing to flush resolver if we provide guidance.
Jonas R (Eng-Runtime): immediate mitigation options: - update TLS to present a compatible cert on old-gw (risky since host is decommissioned) OR - re-point old-gw A -> new-edge LB IP in DNS for a week (safer) OR - ask customer to flush resolver. I prefer DNS re-point + short TTL.
Olivia C (Customer Success): I can push the 'flush' ask to the customer, but corp IT is slow. they'll probably want us to handle it on our side.
Lee K (Eng-SRE): I'll run a DNS publish: create a temporary A record for 54.152.201.98 -> new-edge-lb-1 (IPs) and lower TTL to 60s. doing it now.
Lee K (Eng-SRE): infra change: `dnsctl patch records --name old-gw.example.net --type A --value 3.124.88.11 --ttl 60 --note "temp re-point during cert dep"`
deploy-bot: DNS change queued: CHG-5821. Will apply in ~15s.
Lee K (Eng-SRE): change applied. please verify from customer's side.
Maria S (Support): customer ran curl again after 2m: TLS handshake succeeds, 200 returned, latency ~110ms. they confirm errors dropped to zero. :tada:
Olivia C (Customer Success): customer asks what we will do to prevent future recurrence.
Jonas R (Eng-Runtime): postmortem follow-ups: - ensure decommissioned hosts are removed from all authoritative zones before cert expiry; - add a decomm checklist step: set retired IPs to 301 -> new-edge at DNS/CDN layer for 72h; - build a monitor for stale DNS mappings where CNAME points to retired hostnames; - reduce rollout window TTL to 60s during migrations.
Lee K (Eng-SRE): I've added an alert policy to watch for certificate chain verification failures in edge logs and for mismatched SNI -> cert mappings.
Maria S (Support): closing loop with customer. provided them with MD steps to flush DNS and explained mitigation.
Olivia C (Customer Success): customer extremely appreciative of the quick workaround. requested a follow-up email summarizing steps (I will send).
Jonas R (Eng-Runtime): notes for ops doc: include `dig` sample to debug this class of problem: ```
# from affected client network
dig +short CNAME api.redwood.example.com
dig +trace api.redwood.example.com
curl -v --connect-timeout 10 https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
```
Maria S (Support): adding final notes to support ticket and closing thread.
Lee K (Eng-SRE): postmortem ticket created: PMT-993 (dns-decom-checklist). assigning to eng-infra.
Maria S (Support): resolved. thanks team. :raised_hands:
